item.title: MECHS Add-On
item.creator: Aypierre
item.description:
Craft powerful mechs with the MECHS Add-On.
Mine titanium, craft advanced parts, and assemble your own mech.

TRANSFORM INTO A POWERFUL MECH built for speed, defense, or firepower.
Pilot dynamic mechs with blasters and melee weapons, defeat new mobs, and conquer your world.
item.changelog:
+ Fixed a texture recoloring issue with Iron-Sentinell.
+ Fixed an issue with Boss Mecharacnid’s walking animation.
+ Increased the spawn rate of Titanium Ore.
+ Improved sounds while riding mechs.
+ Improved the targeting system.
+ Fixed several minor bugs.

faqEntries.heading: I have just started: what should I do first?
faqEntries.content: Craft the Guide-Pad with a book and three iron ingots. It is the in-game manual and it walks you through every stage of the add-on. Then go mining: Titanium Ore sits between Y 0 and 52 and needs an iron pickaxe or better. Smelt the raw ore into ingots, the material every recipe asks for.

faqEntries.heading: How do I get the machines that build mechs?
faqEntries.content: Craft the 3D Crafter at a crafting table first: it turns titanium into mech parts. Print the Assembler base, monitor, two towers and two mechanical arms there, place the base on flat open ground and keep interacting to install all five upgrades. Only a finished Assembler can build a mech.

faqEntries.heading: Which mech should I build first?
faqEntries.content: Interact with the finished Assembler to see the exact part list of each mech. Start with Ronin: it is the cheapest, and swaps between brawler fists, a portable cannon and a circular saw that fells trees instantly. Build the Excavator next, as its drill, hammer and laser modes mine titanium far faster.

faqEntries.heading: How do I pilot a mech and change its form?
faqEntries.content: Interact with the mech to climb into the cockpit, then stop moving: the Mech OS menu only opens when you stand still, and it cannot be used in motion or mid-attack. From there you pick the form for the job, like Ronin's saw, the Iron Sentinel's gorilla stance or the Excavator's mining drill.

faqEntries.heading: How do I unlock the Arachnid?
faqEntries.content: The Arachnid cannot be assembled. Craft the Arachnid Summoning Flare in the 3D Crafter and use it on land, in roughly 100 x 100 blocks of clear space: it summons a massive hostile boss. Bring a heavy mech such as the Iron Sentinel, then repair the wrecked carcass it leaves behind to make the Arachnid yours.

faqEntries.heading: What happens when my mech is destroyed?
faqEntries.content: It is not lost. The mech collapses into a broken wreck: interact with it to bring it back online with the required materials, or to dismantle it. To avoid that, carry a Titanium Repair Kit, which heals a mech fully and is crafted from two Red Microchips and two iron ingots. Microchips drop from Mechanized Mobs at night.

howToEntries.heading: Getting Started: Your Guide-Pad and First Supplies
howToEntries.content: You start with two items: the Guide-Pad and a Supply Drop Flare. The Guide-Pad is your manual, covering titanium, the machines, every mech and the monsters that hunt you, plus a settings menu for toggling creative crafting, instant assembly, terrain damage or immortal mechs. If lost, craft another with a book and three iron ingots. Throw the flare on open ground and a supply capsule drops, packed with titanium, iron, energy cores, microchips and food. Then dig between Y 0 and Y 52 with an iron pickaxe for Titanium Ore. Smelt it into ingots and store spares as titanium blocks, because almost every recipe starts here.

howToEntries.heading: Crafting Machines: the 3D Crafter and the Assembler
howToEntries.content: A normal crafting table cannot handle MECHS technology, so first build the 3D Crafter. Craft it at a regular table, place it with a clear 3x3x3 space around it, and interact to open its menu. Every component is sorted by category: energy cores, pistons, armour plates, cannons, each mech's arms and legs, pilot armour, blasters, paint buckets and the Assembler's parts. The Assembler is huge, so find a wide flat area. Place the base, then keep interacting to fit the monitor, two support towers and two mechanical arms. With the fifth piece in place, interacting shows the full parts list for every mech.

howToEntries.heading: Piloting Your Mechs: Six Machines, Many Combat Forms
howToEntries.content: Each machine plays differently. Ronin is the light starter, punching with brawler fists, firing a portable cannon or spinning a saw that fells trees in one hit. Steel Samurai is the duellist: quick spear, sword-and-shield stance or long-range blaster. Iron Sentinel is a walking fortress: arm cannons, gorilla mode for speed, or a shielded turret. Excavator is the miner, with chainsaw, drill, hammer and laser tools. Hive Striker rules the sky with missiles and support bees. Interact to climb aboard, then stand still; the Mech OS menu only opens when you stop moving, and that's where you change form.

howToEntries.heading: Night Raids, Quick Repairs and the Arachnid Boss Fight
howToEntries.content: Once the sun goes down, Mechanized Mobs spawn: titanium versions of zombies, skeletons, creepers, spiders and phantoms, each with 45 health and its own nasty trick, from climbing walls to explosions and aerial strafing. They are also your best source of loot, dropping Red Microchips, pistons, titanium and extra Supply Drop Flares. Two microchips and two iron ingots craft a Titanium Repair Kit that heals a mech back to full. Paint Buckets repaint your mech in nine colours, while pilot armour sets and blasters, reloaded with energy cells, keep you dangerous on foot. The final challenge is the Arachnid: craft its summoning flare, clear a space of about 100 x 100 blocks, defeat the giant boss and repair the carcass to make that MECHS yours!
